## Problem Statement

`detect_regressions()` in `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (line 753) defines a regression as *any* transition away from `completed`/`in_review`:

```python
is_regressed = not (cur_status == "completed" and cur_stage == "in_review")
```

This conflates a **backward slip** (e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/plan_complete`) with the **forward release transition** `completed/in_review` → `completed/done`. The ship skill closes shipped items to `stage: done`; `docs/dev/release-process.md` treats `completed/done` as a terminal (released) state, compatible with `completed/in_review`.

## Observed Impact

Standup window 2026-09-28 06:00 → 2026-09-29 06:00 (SorraAgents). The report's Regressions section listed **80 items**. All 80 were `completed/in_review` in the pre-window snapshot and are now `completed/done` — i.e. all 80 were *released* (release merge `release/dev-to-main-20260928210652`), not regressed. Zero items actually slipped backwards, so the section was 100% false positives and useless.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `detect_regressions()` only flags a genuine backward slip: an item that was `completed`/`in_review` before the window and is now in a non-terminal state (status != `completed`, or stage in `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`). The transition `completed/in_review` → `completed/done` must NOT be flagged.
2. Add regression tests in `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` proving:
   - `completed/in_review` → `completed/done` inside the window is NOT flagged (released);
   - `completed/in_review` → `open/plan_complete` inside the window IS flagged;
   - `completed/in_review` → `blocked/...` inside the window IS flagged;
   - `completed/in_review` → `completed/in_review` is NOT flagged;
   - the existing in-window/out-of-window gating still holds.
3. Existing standup tests pass.

## Provenance

Discovered while investigating the Regressions section of the 2026-09-29 standup report on SorraAgents. Related to SA-0MUFNU2WM00049A9 (operator-precedence fix in the same function), but distinct: that fix gated the predicate on `in_window()`; this bug is the definition of `is_regressed` itself, which still misclassifies the forward `in_review` → `done` release transition.
data.title: Standup skill: regression detection flags released items (in_review -> done) as regressions

Ralph is not present anywhere on disk (no `skill/ralph` directory, no config files, no project references). These references are dead code and stale documentation.

## Dead code in `audit_runner.py`

- `ASSET_CONFIG_PATH` — points to `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json` (missing).
- `RALPH_CONFIG_FILES` — references `.ralph.json` and `ralph.config.json` (neither exists).

- `_deep_merge()` — helper for `_load_config()`.
- `_extract_phase_model_config()` — extracts per-phase model config from loaded JSON.

- `_resolve_phase_model_value()` — resolves a model string from nested config.
- `_coerce_model_str()` — coerces model string.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Remove from `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: `ASSET_CONFIG_PATH`, `RALPH_CONFIG_FILES`, `_load_asset_config()`, `_load_config()`, `_deep_merge()`, `_extract_phase_model_config()`, `_resolve_model_for_phase()`, `_resolve_phase1_model()`, `_resolve_phase_model_value()`, `_coerce_model_str()`, `_model_source()`, and the `--model`/`--phase1-model` CLI flags. Model resolution should fall back directly to `DEFAULT_MODEL`.
2. Remove `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1_model.py` entirely (413 lines of dead tests).
3. Update `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2_benchmark.py` to not call removed functions.
4. Update `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` to remove mocks of `_load_config` / `_resolve_model_for_phase`.

6. Remove references to `.ralph.json` / `ralph.config.json` from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
7. Verify no references to `ralph` (or `.ralph.json` / `ralph.config.json`) remain in code or docs (grep across repo).

# implement.py parent misclassifies soft-deleted children

## Problem
`implement.py parent <parent-id>` treats a child whose `deletedBy` is set (soft-deleted; `status` remains `open`) as implementable. `_classify_child` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` only checks `status` against `TERMINAL_STATUSES` ({in_review, completed, done, deleted}); it never inspects `deletedBy`. As a result `phase_parent` calls `phase_start` on the soft-deleted child, creates a bogus worktree/branch, claims the item `in_progress`, and stops the chain instead of advancing the parent.

## Reproduction
`wl delete <child>` on a child of an epic sets `deletedBy` but leaves `status: open` (verified with SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X / SA-0MUD5U06J009V0EK, both `deletedBy: plan`). Running `implement.py parent SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` then started a worktree for SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X and set it `in-progress`, even though both real children were `completed`.

## Expected
A child with `deletedBy` set must be treated as terminal (`skip-terminal`): never claimed, never given a worktree, and never allowed to block parent advancement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_classify_child` treats `deletedBy` (non-empty) as terminal regardless of `status`.
- [ ] `phase_parent` advances a parent whose only non-terminal statuses are soft-deleted children.
- [ ] Regression test: a soft-deleted child is skipped and the parent advances.
data.title: implement.py parent: soft-deleted children (deletedBy set, status open) are misclassified as implementable and started

# Discord release report: add project elevator pitch and per-release focus paragraphs

## Problem statement

The Discord release notification currently opens with the itemised changelog, which assumes the reader already knows what the project/game is and what this release is about. Channel readers without prior context cannot tell what the project does or what the headline change of the release is without reading the whole changelog.

## Users

- **Release operators / producers** who post release announcements to a shared Discord channel and want the announcement to be self-explanatory.
- **Players / stakeholders / channel readers** who see the announcement and need immediate context.

User stories:

- As a channel reader, I want a 2–3 sentence elevator pitch of the project/game first, so I can understand the announcement without prior context.
- As a release operator, I want a 1–3 sentence summary of the release's main focus, so the headline change is obvious before the itemised changelog.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Ordering and content.** The Discord release embed description is composed of paragraphs in this order: (a) the project elevator pitch (2–3 sentences), (b) the release focus summary (1–3 sentences), (c) the existing project/version line, (d) the changelog section. Verified by unit tests asserting the built payload's paragraph order and content.
- **Pitch sourcing.** The pitch is read from a new `projectDescription` field resolved with the same three-layer precedence as `projectName` (`.worklog/config.private.yaml` → `.worklog/config.yaml` → `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`). When unset, a pitch is generated via the existing DeepSeek LLM pattern from the leading prose of `README.md` (the block before the first `##` heading, capped at ~1000 characters); when generation is unavailable (no API key, LLM error, or missing/unreadable README) the pitch paragraph is omitted. Verified by unit tests with injected config paths and a faked LLM boundary.
- **Focus generation and extraction.** `generate-changelog.js` generates the release focus from the release's work items in its existing LLM pass and persists it in the new `CHANGELOG.md` version section as a machine-extractable marker line (`> **Release focus:** …`) directly under the version heading. `discord-notify.js` extracts that marker, produces the focus paragraph, and removes the marker from the changelog body sent to Discord so the text is not duplicated. When no marker exists, the paragraph is omitted and the changelog renders unchanged.
- **Non-blocking contract preserved.** Every new failure path (missing config, missing API key, LLM error, missing README, missing focus marker) logs an info/warning line and returns without changing the release exit code; the existing behaviours (webhook precedence, skip when unset, HTTP/network failure warning) are unchanged, and the composed description is still truncated to ≤ 4096 characters.
- **Test coverage.** Unit tests cover: pitch from config, pitch from README/LLM fallback, pitch omitted, focus marker generation in the changelog section, focus extraction and de-duplication from the changelog body, focus omitted, paragraph ordering, truncation of the composed description, and config precedence. All LLM/network boundaries are injected (no live network, no live home config or worklog mutation).
- **Documentation and suite.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (`skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`), including the `projectDescription` config schema entry and fallback semantics. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependencies** — Node.js 18+ built-ins only (`fetch`, `AbortSignal`), consistent with `discord-notify.js` today.
- **LLM access** uses the existing `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` + DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible endpoint with the graceful `null` fallback. The shared caller is extracted into a small `llm.js` module; `discord-notify.js` must **not** import `generate-changelog.js` (it runs `git rev-parse` at module import).
- **No tracked-file mutation at release time** — the README-derived pitch is generated on the fly and not persisted to `.worklog/config.yaml`, avoiding a dirty worktree mid-release (which could interfere with the post-merge dev sync). Documented assumption; persistence can be a follow-up.
- **English:** all docs/comments must use UK English.
- **Existing notification behaviour** (webhook precedence, skip when unset, HTTP failure non-blocking) must be unchanged.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` builds the embed: title `<projectName> Release v<version>`, description `**<projectName> v<version>**` + changelog section, fields Version / Tag / Date / PR. It has a minimal YAML subset parser supporting top-level scalars and one level of nesting.
- `projectName` is resolved from `.worklog/config.private.yaml` → `.worklog/config.yaml` → `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` (SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD).
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` runs a per-work-item LLM pass (`callLlm`, DeepSeek, `null` fallback) and `generateReleaseSection()` emits `## vX.Y.Z (date)` followed by `### Features` / `### Bug Fixes` / `### Other`.
- `run-release.js` calls `sendReleaseNotification({version, prUrl, projectRoot})` after merge verification, never on `--dry-run`.

## Desired change

- New config field `projectDescription` (top-level scalar in `.worklog/config.yaml`) resolved with the same precedence chain as `projectName`; documented in the ship reference and example config.
- New shared module `skill/ship/scripts/llm.js` exporting `callLlm(messages, opts)` (moved from `generate-changelog.js`, which imports it from there).
- `generate-changelog.js`: request a 1–3 sentence focus paragraph from the LLM over the release's categorised items and persist it as `> **Release focus:** …` directly under the version heading; omit when the LLM is unavailable.
- `discord-notify.js`: extract the `> **Release focus:**` marker (and remove it from the changelog body); resolve the pitch (`projectDescription`, else README/LLM, else omit); compose the description as pitch → focus → project/version line → changelog; truncate the composed description at 4096 characters.

## **Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — pitch resolution (+ README/LLM fallback), focus extraction, new description order; keep existing config helpers.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` — release-focus generation and section marker.
- `skill/ship/scripts/llm.js` — new shared LLM caller (extracted; graceful `null` fallback).
- `tests/unit/test-discord-notify.mjs` — ordering / fallback / extraction tests.
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-query.mjs` (or a new `test-generate-changelog-focus.mjs`) — focus marker generation tests.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — mirrored coverage.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — documentation.
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — optional `projectDescription` example/pitch for this repository.

## Related work

- **Ship skill: send Discord message with release details + changelog on successful release (SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z)** — the notification feature this extends; its non-blocking/truncation contracts carry over.
- **Ship report to discord needs titling (SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD)** — introduced `projectName` resolution; the closest precedent for `projectDescription`.
- **Move release-notification (Discord) webhook secret into a gitignored per-project `.worklog/config.private.yaml` (SA-0MUF833QL001WJXD)** — established the config precedence chain.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "create it with LLM from the start of the README" means generate the pitch at release time, not persist it. Rationale: persisting would dirty the tracked worktree during the release pipeline (risking the post-merge `dev` sync). *Producer action: confirm; if persistence is wanted, raise a follow-up work item.*
- **Assumption:** "the start of the README" means the leading prose block before the first `##` heading; when the README is missing or has no prose, generation is skipped and the pitch omitted.
- **Risk:** LLM-generated focus/pitch may be bland or misleading. Mitigation: bounded length (pitch 2–3 sentences, focus 1–3), focus persisted in `CHANGELOG.md` for review, omission on failure, and config text always wins over generation.
- **Risk:** extra LLM latency/cost in the release path. Mitigation: one focus call per release (piggybacking the existing changelog LLM pass) plus at most one pitch call; bounded 30 s timeout; non-blocking.
- **Risk:** truncation could cut the pitch/focus paragraphs. Mitigation: prompt-enforced brevity; existing 4096-char truncation retained.
- **Risk (scope creep):** extending generation to all projects' configs. Mitigation: feature is config-driven/opt-in; only the fallback generator is universal. Extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Source of the project elevator pitch?" — Answer (operator): "A (if not present then create it with LLM from the start of the README)". Source: interactive reply. Implication: `projectDescription` config field with README/LLM fallback; omission when generation unavailable.
- Q2: "Source of the per-release focus paragraph?" — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply. Implication: LLM-generated during the existing `generate-changelog.js` pass, persisted in the `CHANGELOG.md` version section, extracted by `discord-notify.js`.
- Q3: "Behaviour when a pitch/focus paragraph is unavailable?" — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply. Implication: omit the paragraph silently; preserve the non-blocking release semantics and the existing notification content.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPDZEDED005YYIJ** – Docs: Update agent/ship.md & release docs (completed)
- **SA-0MQ1O0XIQ00345VM** – Include pi command and work item title in Ralph event/Discord notifications (completed)
- **SA-0MLK57HG10JDXRJA** – Docs for implement preflight + new skill (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, first, followed, high, initial (+15 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: add, first, focus, followed, high (+14 more)
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — matched: add, first, focus, followed, high (+13 more)
data.title: Discord release report: add project elevator pitch and per-release focus paragraphs

# Problem

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 introduced conditional header/conclusion in `render_report.py` — any unmet AC triggers "incomplete". The intake SKILL.md was fixed (SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z) by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. **Every other report-rendering skill still uses placeholder `--ac` values.** Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to say "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR establishes the design contract: the report's Acceptance Criteria table is for the *skill session's* own success criteria. Work-item ACs belong in the separate "Use Cases" section that SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR adds.

## Users

- **Agents** producing skill reports — they need a clear contract for which ACs to pass.
- **Operators** reading reports — they expect the report to reflect the skill session's success, not the work item's implementation status.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every report-rendering SKILL.md (15 skills) passes concrete skill-session ACs in its final-step `--ac` block, all "met" on successful execution.
2. Each SKILL.md's final step includes a one-line note distinguishing skill-session ACs from work-item feature ACs.
3. `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` extended with a guard test asserting each final-step block contains at least one concrete `--ac "...|met"` example (not placeholder).
4. `skill/report/SKILL.md` caller rules strengthened to document the skill-session vs work-item AC distinction.
5. Full test suite green.

## Children

| Child | Skills Covered | Dependencies |
|-------|---------------|--------------|
| Child A | report SKILL.md caller contract | — (blocks B, C) |
| Child B | plan, find-related, effort-and-risk, triage, author-command, cleanup, code-review, refactor, machine-hygiene, resolve-pr-comments | A |
| Child C | test, ship, implement, audit | A |
| Child D | regression guard test | B, C |
| Child E | verify full suite + sync | D |

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Backwards compatibility**: `--ac` values are consumed only by the report renderer; changing them does not affect any CLI or library caller.
- **Implement/audit semantics**: these skills evaluate the work item's ACs, which is a legitimate use of `--ac`. The fix documents this explicitly and coordinates with SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR (Use Cases section) for work-item AC display.
- **Scope**: changes are SKILL.md (docs) only — no code changes. The guard test is a doc-convention check.
- **Existing ACs**: intake was fixed independently (SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z); the epic covers the remaining 14 skills.

## Key Files

- `skill/*/SKILL.md` — final-step blocks for 15 skills
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — extend with AC-concreteness guard
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — strengthen caller rules

# Problem

The report SKILL.md's caller rules state "AC verdicts come from the calling skill's own evaluation" but do not distinguish *skill-session* ACs (the skill's own success criteria) from *work-item* ACs (the feature being implemented). All 14 report-rendering skills still use placeholder `--ac` values, so agents pass the work item's feature ACs — causing the report to incorrectly show "incomplete" when the skill session succeeded.

SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR establishes the contract: `--ac` = skill-session ACs; work-item ACs go to the "Use Cases" section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/report/SKILL.md` caller rules explicitly state: "The `--ac` table records the **skill session's** own success criteria (e.g. brief drafted, children created, build green). Work-item feature ACs are surfaced in the **Use Cases** section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR), not in the `--ac` table."
2. Add a second worked example (in the Example rendered report section) showing a non-plan skill (e.g. audit or intake) passing skill-session ACs, to make the distinction concrete.
3. The placeholder `--ac` block in the invocation example is updated to show explicit skill-session ACs with a note: `# Skill-session deliverables; not the work item's feature ACs`.
4. No change to `render_report.py` code — this is SKILL.md only.
5. Full test suite green.

# Problem

All 10 planning/analysis/maintenance skills use placeholder `--ac` values in their final-step `render_report` blocks. Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to show "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 made `render_report()` derive session status from AC verdicts: any unmet → "incomplete". SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z fixed intake by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. This child fixes the remaining 10 skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each SKILL.md's final-step `--ac` block replaced with concrete skill-session deliverable ACs (4 per skill for skills with multiple deliverables; 3 for simpler skills).
2. Each final-step block includes a one-line note: "> **Note:** ACs record the *skill session's* own deliverables — not the work item's feature acceptance criteria."
3. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
4. Full test suite green (existing tests unaffected by doc-only changes).
5. No new `--ac` lines change the renderer's behaviour; all `--ac` values use the "met" verdict on success.

The 4 operational/delivery skills (test, ship, implement, audit) use placeholder `--ac` values. For test/ship the session ACs are the operational deliverables (suite run, failures triaged / release promoted, audit performed). For implement/audit, the semantics are different — these skills evaluate the work item's ACs as part of their session, which is a legitimate use of `--ac`. This child clarifies the distinction and aligns with SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR.

1. **test** (`skill/test/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: full test suite executed, failures parsed into triage records, critical failures triaged into work items, report rendered.

Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."

Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."

# Problem

There is no automated guard against future regressions of the placeholder-`--ac` pattern. Agents adding new report-rendering skills (or editing existing ones) might again use `--ac "<AC# description>|…|met"` placeholders instead of concrete skill-session deliverables.

SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S already added `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` which checks that every work-item skill has the final-step section and invokes `render_report`. This child extends it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Extend `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` with a new test class `TestReportACConcreteness`:
   - `test_all_final_step_acs_are_concrete`: asserts each work-item skill's `--ac` lines contain at least one literal `|met` value (no placeholders like `<AC# description>`).
   - `test_all_final_steps_have_semantics_note`: asserts each work-item skill's final-step block contains a note distinguishing skill-session ACs from work-item feature ACs (search for patterns like "skill session" or "own deliverable" in the final-step block).
2. Add the new test class to the existing test file (no new test files).
3. All 6 existing hygiene tests still pass.
4. Full test suite green.
